questions.question_text: What is the exact value of $\cos 75^{\circ}$?

options.why: Forgot the sign flip in the cosine sum identity, calculating $\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$ instead of $\cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B$.
Omitted the $\sqrt{2}$ factor in the denominator from $\cos 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Swapped the order of terms, subtracting $\cos 45^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ}$ from $\sin 45^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ}$.
Added the $\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6}$ terms instead of cancelling them during subtraction.
Used $\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ instead of $\frac{1}{2}$ when evaluating $2\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$.
Subtracted in reverse order, introducing an extra negative sign.

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) - \sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$
$= \left(\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + \cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right) - \left(\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6} - \cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$
$= 2\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$
$= 2\cos x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$= \cos x$

questions.question_text: What is the exact value of $\sin 80^{\circ}\cos 20^{\circ} - \cos 80^{\circ}\sin 20^{\circ}$?

options.why: Applied the cosine difference identity $\cos(80^{\circ}-20^{\circ})=\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}$ instead of sine.
Added the angles as $\sin(80^{\circ}+20^{\circ})$ instead of subtracting them.
Confused the compound formula with orthogonal angle identities.

questions.question_text: Given acute angles $A$ and $B$ with $\cos A = \frac{4}{5}$ and $\sin B = \frac{12}{13}$, find the exact value of $\cos(A + B)$.

options.why: Used the sine compound identity $\sin(A+B)$ instead of the cosine compound identity $\cos(A+B)$.
Used addition $\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B = \frac{20+36}{65} = \frac{56}{65}$, forgetting the cosine sign flip.
Swapped $\sin A$ and $\cos A$ values during calculation.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Since }A\text{ and }B\text{ are acute:}$
$\sin A = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2}} = \frac{3}{5}$
$\cos B = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{12}{13}\right)^{2}} = \frac{5}{13}$
$\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B$
$= \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) - \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)$
$= \frac{20}{65} - \frac{36}{65}$
$= -\frac{16}{65}$

options.why: Used a minus sign in the denominator instead of a plus sign for the tangent difference formula.
Subtracted $\tan x$ from $\tan\frac{\pi}{4}$ in the numerator instead of $\tan x - \tan\frac{\pi}{4}$.
Assumed the tangent operator distributes across subtraction.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
$= \frac{\tan x - \tan\frac{\pi}{4}}{1 + \tan x\tan\frac{\pi}{4}}$
$= \frac{\tan x - 1}{1 + (\tan x)(1)}$
$= \frac{\tan x - 1}{1 + \tan x}$

questions.question_text: What is the exact value of $\tan\frac{\pi}{12}$ using $\frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{6}$?

options.why: Added the tangent ratios in the numerator, finding $\tan\frac{5\pi}{12}$ instead of $\tan\frac{\pi}{12}$.
Omitted the denominator $1 + \tan\frac{\pi}{4}\tan\frac{\pi}{6}$ entirely.
Failed to rationalise the denominator $(\sqrt{3}+1)$ correctly.

questions.question_text: Given that $\tan\theta = 3$ and $\tan\varphi = \frac{1}{2}$, what is the exact value of $\tan(\theta + \varphi)$?

options.why: Used $1 + \tan\theta\tan\varphi$ in the denominator instead of $1 - \tan\theta\tan\varphi$, missing the negative sign.
Calculated the denominator as $1 + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{2}$, giving $\frac{7/2}{5/2} = \frac{7}{5}$.
Divided $\frac{7}{2}$ by $-1$ instead of by $1 - \frac{3}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$.
Swapped variables $A$ and $B$, simplifying to $\frac{\sin A}{\cos A}$ instead of $\frac{\sin B}{\cos B}$.
Inverted the quotient, calculating $\frac{\cos B}{\sin B}$.
Subtracted the numerator in reverse order as $\cos(A+B)-\cos(A-B)$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Numerator: } (\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B) - (\cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B) = 2\sin A\sin B$
$\text{Denominator: } (\sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B) + (\sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B) = 2\sin A\cos B$
$\frac{2\sin A\sin B}{2\sin A\cos B} = \frac{\sin B}{\cos B}$
$= \tan B$
